Let \(d\) be the number of digits of \(r\). Then
\[
q\cdot 10^d + r + 3 = p^2.
\]
If \(p\) is odd, then \(p^2-3\) is even. But \(q\cdot 10^d\) is even, so
\[
q\cdot 10^d+r
\]
has the parity of \(r\). Since \(r\) is prime, the only even possibility is \(r=2\). Thus \(d=1\), and
\[
p^2-3 = 10q+2.
\]
So
\[
p^2 = 10q+5 = 5(2q+1).
\]
Hence \(5\mid p^2\), so \(p=5\). Then \(q=2\), which is prime, and \(22+3=25=5^2\).

The prime \(p=2\) gives \(p^2-3=1\), impossible.

Therefore the only possible value is
\[
\boxed{5}.
\]
